svg.aria-label: A symptom map for textures that do not show in Blender. A bright magenta surface means Blender cannot find the image file; fix with File, External Data, Find Missing Files. Grey and untextured everywhere means the viewport is in Solid shading; press Z and choose Material Preview. One flat colour over the whole mesh means there is no UV map or the UVs are collapsed; in Edit Mode press U and choose Smart UV Project. Looking right until you render means the image texture node is not linked to Base Color; check the link in the Shading workspace. A texture that is present but stretched means unapplied object scale or uneven UV scale; apply scale with Control A and re-unwrap. Four of the five are a single click; only the UV one takes real time.
svg.text: WHAT YOU SEE — AND WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG

g.text: Surface is bright magenta
The colour Blender uses for an image it cannot load
Blender cannot find the image file
It was moved, renamed, or never packed
External Data
Find Missing Files
Grey and untextured, everywhere
Every object in the file looks the same
The viewport is in Solid shading
Nothing is wrong with the material at all
Press Z
Material Preview
One flat colour over the whole mesh
Looks untextured, but the texture is loaded
No UV map, or UVs collapsed
The mesh samples a single texel
Edit Mode, U
Smart UV Project
Looks right until you render
Fine in the viewport, gone in the F12 result
Node not linked to Base Color
Added, positioned, never connected
Shading workspace
Follow the noodle
Present, but stretched or tiled wrong
The texture is clearly there and clearly off
Unapplied object scale, or UV scale
The mesh was scaled in Object Mode
Ctrl+A, Scale
Then re-unwrap

svg.text: Work down the list in order. Four of the five are a single click — only the UV one costs you real time.
